label: A possible contingent-free past from possible founded coming-to-be
description: New non-transcription conditional support option for premise A3 of the modal spine to God's existence. In the accessible history, the contingent individual x present at the founded moment t was absent at an earlier moment s. Because there is no endless descent below t, some moment m at or below s has no strictly earlier moment (classical case split along accessibility of the strict order). Any contingent concrete individual present at m would need a still earlier moment of absence, which m lacks; so m is free of contingent concrete individuals and lies strictly before t, where x is present. No frame condition, presence contract, inertness of emptiness or causal relation is used. The single premise is OPEN; it is a possibility claim and is stronger than the conclusion. This repairs, for contingent concrete things under an earlier-absence reading and a founded past, the quantifier shift the corpus records as invalid in general; nothing is attributed to a source. No premise truth is established.

research_comparisons.conditions: None beyond the two statements themselves: possibleContingentFreePast derives the negation of the rival from the target, with the three permitted Mathlib axioms.
research_comparisons.scope: Same History carrier, Concrete predicate, preorder of times, frame and selected world.
research_comparisons.coverage: The initial-state rival as encoded (no accessible contingent-free moment before a contingent-populated one); not every philosophical view called an initial-state view.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: Checked incompatibility, not exhaustiveness: both statements can fail together.
research_comparisons.next_step: The rival's holder must deny that founded coming-to-be is possible: in every accessible history either some contingent concrete thing never came to be or no populated moment has a founded past. Test each horn against the causal-finitism and brute-foundation results.
